name: Timeouts and circuit breakers
needs: my app hangs when a third-party API is slow
one slow service takes down my whole app
retries ran up a huge bill when an API was down
summary: A timeout puts a limit on how long you wait for another service. A circuit breaker watches for repeated failures and, once there are too many, stops calling that service for a while and fails right away. Together they keep one slow dependency from tying up your whole app or running up a bill.
need_when: Your app calls payment, email, AI or other third-party APIs during a request.
You have retries, and a long outage could turn them into a flood of calls.
skip_when: Calls that only happen in background jobs with their own timeout, where waiting longer is fine.

ways.title: Timeouts on every outbound call
ways.how: Set a timeout in your HTTP client (requests timeout=, fetch with AbortSignal.timeout, SDK timeout options). Most clients wait forever by default.
ways.tradeoff: The biggest win for the least work. Pick numbers from how slow the service really gets.

ways.title: A circuit breaker library
ways.how: opossum (Node), pybreaker (Python) or resilience4j (Java) wrapped around the calls that matter.
ways.tradeoff: Stops hammering a service that is down. Another thing to tune and monitor.

ways.title: Move slow calls off the request
ways.how: Put the call in a background job, show a pending state, and let the job retry with backoff.
ways.tradeoff: Users never wait on a third party. Needs a job queue and a way to show results later.

prompt:
Add timeouts and a circuit breaker to this app's outbound calls to [Stripe / OpenAI / email provider / other APIs].

Requirements:
- Find every outbound HTTP or SDK call and give it an explicit timeout: [5] seconds for user-facing requests, longer only where the work needs it.
- Cap retries at [2] with exponential backoff and jitter. Never retry inside a loop that is itself retried.
- Wrap [the slow or flaky service] in a circuit breaker that opens after [5] failures in a row, fails fast for [30] seconds, then lets one test call through.
- When the breaker is open, return a clear message or a fallback instead of an error page.
- Log each timeout and every time the breaker opens or closes.
- Use [opossum / pybreaker / the existing HTTP client's options].

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Pointing [service] at an address that never answers makes the call fail within the set timeout, not hang.
2. A slow external service doesn't make unrelated pages slow, checked with a quick load test.
3. After [5] failures in a row the breaker opens and calls fail fast without hitting the service.
4. Once the service is back, the breaker closes again on its own and calls succeed.
acceptance_checks: Pointing [service] at an address that never answers makes the call fail within the set timeout, not hang.
A slow external service doesn't make unrelated pages slow, checked with a quick load test.
After [5] failures in a row the breaker opens and calls fail fast without hitting the service.
Once the service is back, the breaker closes again on its own and calls succeed.
if_you_skip_it: One slow API ties up every worker and your whole site goes down with it. Retries against a dead service can pile up into thousands of calls and a surprise bill.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal sets explicit timeouts on its outbound calls: 10 seconds for each webhook delivery, with the DNS lookup capped at 5 seconds, and 60 seconds with one retry for voice memo transcription, which then tells the user to try again or type instead. It does not use a circuit breaker.
